sections.title: Med-Qwen-3.5-4B-Instruct
sections.desc: The 4.2B clinical reasoning model Med-Qwen: domain-adaptive pretraining and DoRA fine-tuning, benchmark scores against MedGemma and its Qwen base.
asks: What PubMedQA score did Med-Qwen get?
How was Med-Qwen trained?
How does it compare to MedGemma?
chunks: Project Med-Qwen-3.5-4B-Instruct (Oct 2026): Delivered Med-Qwen-3.5-4B-Instruct, a 4.2B clinical reasoning SLM that outscored MedGemma-1.5-4B-it on all six clinical benchmarks (PubMedQA 66.20, MedQA USMLE 67.95), by domain-adaptive pretraining over Qwen3.5-4B-Base then a 2,700-step DoRA (r=64, alpha=128) supervised fine-tuning pass over an 11-stream clinical reasoning mixture (~276M tokens).

Project Med-Qwen-3.5-4B-Instruct (Oct 2026): Scored PubMedQA 66.20 against 45.60 for Qwen3.5-4B-Base, with GPQA Diamond 50.51, MMLU Med 80.72, MedMCQA 33.20 and AfriMed-QA 64.80 under zero-shot greedy inference with normalized choice log-probabilities.

Med-Qwen RLVR stage: Cut medical reasoning length about 7x (456 to 66 tokens) at matching MedQA accuracy by training a GRPO RLVR adapter on Qwen3.5-4B with rule-based accuracy, format and length rewards.
Result - PubMedQA, Med-Qwen vs base: 66.20 vs 45.60 (Med-Qwen-3.5-4B, 2026). Method: zero-shot greedy inference with normalized choice log-probabilities.
